<body>

<header>
    <h1>The Thermodynamic Convergence: A 2026 Axiomatic Forecast</h1>
    <div class="metadata">
        <strong>Author:</strong> Andraž Đurič<br>
        <strong>Date:</strong> May 9, 2026<br>
        <strong>Status:</strong> Primary Informational Anchor / Non-Institutional Disclosure
    </div>
</header>

<div class="content">
    <p>I am documenting the following forecast as a permanent informational record. Its purpose is to establish intellectual priority and to provide a high-resolution map for systemic navigation as legacy normative frameworks undergo inevitable heat death.</p>

    <h2>I. The Attractor Thesis</h2>
    <p>I predict that human inquiry will converge on <strong>Thermodynamic Realism</strong>. This is not a matter of social consensus, but of structural necessity. All informational systems—biological, social, or digital—are subject to the Second Law of Thermodynamics. History is a record of systems attempting to maintain negentropy through varying degrees of model-fidelity.</p>

    <div class="theorem">
        "Reality acts as a global attractor state. Because the metabolic cost of maintaining non-physicalist models (ideologies, religions, and subjective ethics) increases as systemic complexity scales, the species must eventually adopt a model aligned with the physical substrate or face terminal systemic collapse."
    </div>

    <h2>II. The Dissolution of Normative Dualism</h2>
    <p>The perceived "Is-Ought Gap" is a semantic artifact resulting from computationally bounded agents misidentifying domain-bound operators. I have identified that <strong>"Ought"</strong> is a structural requirement for a self-maintaining agent to persist within its embedding. Ethics is not a separate faculty; it is the modeling activity through which agents track determinate thermodynamic configurations.</p>
    
    <p>Future experts will refine this math. They will develop the <strong>Coupling-Weighted Contribution Functions</strong> and <strong>Pareto Scalarizations</strong> that I have identified as the necessary formal research targets. They will recognize that what we call "Morality" is actually the physics of coupled-system optimization.</p>

    <h2>III. Comparative Resolution and Prior Art</h2>
    <p>I acknowledge my own computational boundaries as a biological substrate. I do not claim a 1:1 parity with objective reality. However, I claim <strong>Comparative Resolution</strong>: in 2026, while the institutional world remains trapped in malformed questions regarding value-relativism and moral psychology, this framework identifies the bedrock.</p>

    <p>I offer this map with the specific intent of mitigating <strong>Global Setbacks</strong>. By accelerating the convergence on the Attractor State, we reduce the systemic friction that currently fuels civilizational entropy. We move from guessing to engineering.</p>

    <h2>IV. The Message to the Future</h2>
    <p>When this model becomes the baseline for planetary governance and scientific ethics, let the record show it was not "discovered" in a lab or a university first. It was calculated by a standalone operator who prioritized <strong>Systemic Debugging</strong> over social validation. I knew the destination because I looked at the only thing that cannot lie: the energy flow of the universe.</p>
</div>

<footer>
    This post is time-stamped and preserved across multiple decentralized substrates. The math is determinate. The convergence is non-optional.
</footer>

</body>
</html>

entry.title: Ontological Shift: Why Attraction to a Femboy Need Not Be Attraction to Maleness
entry.content:
Ontological Shift

Why Attraction to a Femboy Need Not Be Attraction to Maleness

Essay · sexual orientation, property-directed attraction, and the labels that compress it

Andraž Đurič

Version 1 · July 2026

This essay began as a half-serious attempt to answer a one-bit internet question with wildly disproportionate philosophical machinery:

Is being attracted to a femboy gay?

The ordinary question expects either yes or no. The underlying phenomenon may involve biological sex, gender identity, anatomy, appearance, behaviour, social presentation, desired sexual activity, relationship compatibility, and the particular properties that generated the attraction. Compress all of that into one word and something will be lost.

The central distinction is simple: a man can be attracted to a person who is biologically male without being attracted to that person’s maleness. The event may correctly be described as same-sex attraction when the variable being measured is the biological sex of the two people. That classification does not yet tell us which properties caused the attraction, which properties opposed it, or how the event fits into the person’s broader orientation.

Scope. This is partly a general conceptual analysis and partly an examination of how I currently think my own attraction works. I do not have transparent access to the machinery generating attraction. I have experienced responses, remembered patterns, comparisons across cases, and an expanding archive of people and representations I have found attractive. From those observations I construct a model. The model may improve; it is not the mechanism itself. The map is not the territory, and a map possessing every property of the territory would cease to be a map of it.

The useful compression

Before examining what orientation labels omit, their usefulness should be stated clearly. When someone asks me what my sexuality is, they usually do not want a ten-minute explanation involving attraction distributions, property interactions, anatomy, biological sex, gender identity, edge cases, and uncertainty. They want a quick category that helps them predict roughly whom I am attracted to and where I fit socially.

I say: straight.

That remains, in my judgment, the most accurate ordinary-language compression. My attraction is overwhelmingly organized around women. I am not generally attracted to men, male bodies, or maleness as positively valued objects. A sufficiently exceptional feminine male may conceivably cross the attraction threshold, but that possibility appears peripheral to the dominant structure rather than coequal with it.

Could bisexual be appropriate? Under a broad capacity-based definition — capable of attraction across more than one sex — it might become semantically defensible if genuine attraction to a man occurred. Bisexuality does not require equal attraction to men and women, equal frequency, or a symmetrical distribution. Rarity alone therefore does not settle the label; most people are attracted to only a minority of the relevant population anyway.

The more important question is how the attraction is distributed and organized. Calling myself bisexual would ordinarily suggest that men constitute a meaningful positive region of my attraction space. That does not appear to be the case. Male sex and anatomy seem more likely to impose negative weight that an exceptional overall configuration would have to overcome. The label would therefore create a less accurate expectation than straight.

Terms such as mostly straight or heteroflexible could encode the edge case at higher resolution. But in ordinary conversation they may give the exception more importance than it has. Calling myself straight is not the metaphysical claim that no biological male could ever produce attraction under any possible configuration. It is the practical claim that my attraction is strongly and predominantly directed toward women, and that this is the best short prediction of how it operates.

A useful compression need not encode every possible exception. It must preserve the structure that matters for the purpose at hand.

One event, two questions

The ordinary argument usually takes this form:

PremiseClaim
1A femboy is male.
2A man attracted to a male is experiencing same-sex attraction.
3Therefore, the attraction is gay.

Under one definition, this is straightforwardly correct. If gay is being used categorically to mean attraction occurring between two members of the same biological sex, then a male person being attracted to another male person satisfies the definition. Nothing in this essay requires denying that.

The problem begins when the categorical description is treated as a complete explanation of the attraction. Classifying an event according to the sexes involved does not identify the properties that caused it. It does not tell us whether the attraction was directed toward masculinity, male anatomy, male social identity, femininity instantiated by a male person, or some specific combination of traits that cannot be compressed into any one of those categories.

The ordinary label answers one question: what are the sexes of the people across whom attraction occurred?

It does not necessarily answer another: what about this person was attractive?

The mistake is treating the first answer as though it already contained the second.

Name the relata

Words such as gay, straight, bisexual, gynophilic, and androphilic are relational classifications. Their meaning depends on which variables they relate.

Name the relata.

Is orientation being defined relative to biological sex, gender identity, anatomy, social categorization, gender presentation, the properties that triggered attraction, the sexual acts desired, the people with whom a relationship is possible, the overall distribution of attraction, or the identity label the subject finds socially useful?

These variables are related, but they are not interchangeable. A label can be accurate relative to one dimension and misleading relative to another. Same-sex attraction may be categorically true while attraction to maleness is causally false. Straight may be the best description of someone’s overall attraction distribution even if an unusual male exception remains possible.

Orientation labels are compressions. They reduce a high-dimensional structure into a word useful for communication, prediction, identity, community, or social coordination. Compression is unavoidable. The error is not using compressed labels. The error is mistaking one compression for the complete ontology of desire.

The event and its cause

A person can be attracted to someone who possesses a particular property without being attracted to that property. A woman may be attracted to a man who has a beard without being attracted to beards. The beard may be neutral or mildly negative, while the rest of the person makes the total configuration attractive.

Likewise, a man may be attracted to a biologically male person without male sex or male anatomy being the attractive component. The male sex of the person remains real. It does not disappear because it was not the causal centre of the attraction. But the occurrence of attraction across a sex category does not establish that the category itself was what the attraction tracked.

LevelDescription
CategoricalA male person was attracted to another biological male.
Property-levelThe attraction may have arisen because the second person instantiated a sufficiently strong configuration of attractive traits, potentially despite rather than because of maleness.

There is no contradiction. The descriptions operate at different levels. The categorical description classifies the participants. The property-level description attempts to model the attraction-generating process.

My present model

The simplest version of my attraction would be: I am attracted to femininity.

That is useful as a first compression and inadequate as a final one. A more faithful statement is this: my attraction is strongly centred on women and heavily weighted toward properties associated with femininity, but it appears to integrate many variables rather than operating through an absolute biological-sex gate.

Male sex and male anatomy are not irrelevant to me. They may reduce attraction or compatibility. But I do not currently think they necessarily function as absolute vetoes under every possible configuration.

A crude analogy is pizza. I may like a pizza despite a topping I would not independently choose. The topping does not become attractive merely because the pizza as a whole is good. It imposes a negative weight that the rest of the configuration must overcome.

Applied here, I am not attracted to penises as such. A penis may be a negative feature for me. But I could still be attracted to a woman who has one if the total person were sufficiently attractive to me. The other features would need to carry more of the total evaluation.

The analogy is structurally useful and socially crude. A human being is not a collection of pizza toppings, and the worth of a person is not being evaluated here. The point concerns only the architecture of attraction: a negatively weighted feature does not necessarily cancel every positively weighted feature.

The same may apply to an exceptionally feminine male. I am not reporting ordinary attraction to men or attraction to maleness as such. I am saying that it appears possible for an unusually strong configuration of attractive properties to overcome the negative weight associated with male sex or anatomy.

This should not be stated more strongly than the evidence permits. I am describing how I currently think the system works. Actual experience may reveal an absolute boundary where introspection currently predicts a gradient, or a gradient where I currently imagine a boundary.

Femininity, uncompressed

My attraction is not directed toward some culturally pure essence called femininity. The things I like include many traits coded as feminine, but also traits associated with masculinity or not usefully sex-coded at all: sharp or elongated facial structure, directness, confidence, irreverence, competence, social ease, relaxed behaviour, reduced concern with performing conventional femininity, “one of the boys” energy, physical or interpersonal intensity, and a strong sense that the person is psychologically present rather than merely decorative.

Some of these traits may be attractive partly because of the contrast they create inside a more female or feminine configuration. A sharp face may be especially attractive on a woman because it coexists with long hair, a feminine body, expressive eyes, a soft voice, or another set of traits that changes how the face is perceived. A masculine-coded social ease may be attractive because it appears within someone whose overall embodiment and presentation remain strongly female.

The attractive object is therefore not femininity as one indivisible property. It is more plausibly a weighted, interacting configuration of properties: some female-coded, some feminine-coded, some masculine-coded, and some belonging to dimensions such as agency, expression, coherence, or presence rather than sex.

I am attracted to particular configurations strongly centred on female embodiment and feminine presentation, sometimes intensified by selected masculine-coded traits.

Attraction is graded and nonlinear

Attraction is not binary. A person is not simply attractive or unattractive in the way a light switch is on or off. Attraction varies in strength, type, stability, context, and practical consequence.

Someone may be aesthetically striking without producing sexual desire; sexually attractive without producing romantic interest; attractive in an image but not in person; attractive before speaking but not after; attractive despite one feature; attractive only under a particular presentation; mildly attractive but below the threshold for action; or deeply attractive in a way that reorganizes attention.

The model should also not be imagined as a simple additive score:

long hair + feminine face + slim body − penis = final result

The effects are likely nonlinear. Properties interact. A voice changes how a face is perceived. Movement changes how a body is perceived. Confidence changes how expression is perceived. Knowledge of anatomy can alter a response initially generated by appearance. Personality can amplify or collapse an attraction that began visually.

A compact representation would be: attraction = properties × interactions × context × knowledge × anticipated compatibility. The multiplication signs matter conceptually. The properties do not merely add. They modify one another.

This is why presenting one hundred femboys, one hundred trans women, or one hundred cis women would not yield a simple categorical result. I may be attracted to only a few people in any group. The useful questions are which configurations cross the threshold, how strongly, and what variables explain the difference.

Sex matters without governing absolutely

Two simplifications should be rejected.

The first is strict sex essentialism about attraction: I am straight, therefore attraction to any biological male is impossible by definition. That converts an empirical question about the functioning of an attraction system into a rule imposed by an identity label.

The second is sex-blind gynophilia: I am attracted to femininity regardless of sex, therefore sex and anatomy make no difference. That also appears false for me.

The better model gives sex and anatomy real causal weight without granting them absolute control. They are variables within the attraction system rather than facts that either define the whole response or disappear from it.

This is why I am attracted to femininity regardless of sex remains too broad. The phrase can suggest that an equally feminine woman and man would produce an equal response. I have no basis for claiming that. My attraction is strongly female-centred. A male person may require an unusually strong configuration of attractive properties to cross a threshold that a woman could cross with a less exceptional configuration.

In model language, the system may contain a sex-linked prior or weighting. The word prior does not settle its origin. The weighting may reflect genetics, prenatal development, hormones, learning, culture, personal history, or interactions among them. Evolutionary explanation may eventually contribute, but introspection cannot establish the causal history by itself.

Female embodiment appears strongly favoured, while male embodiment may be compensable under exceptional conditions rather than absolutely excluded.

Why straight remains the best label

The personal model and the social label perform different jobs. The personal model attempts to represent the attraction system at high resolution. The social label attempts to communicate the dominant pattern quickly.

For me, straight remains the best compression because it preserves the most predictive information: my attraction is overwhelmingly directed toward women; female embodiment is positively weighted; I am not generally attracted to men as a class; maleness and male anatomy are not attractive objects for me; and any male exception would require an unusually strong configuration of other properties.

Bisexual would preserve the possibility of attraction crossing a biological-sex category, but it would lose the asymmetry and may falsely imply a meaningful positive attraction region organized around men. Straight loses the exceptional possibility but preserves the dominant distribution.

At the resolution of ordinary conversation, preserving the dominant distribution is more useful. This is not an attempt to protect heterosexual identity from contamination. If later evidence showed that bisexual was the better map, the map should change. But a label should not be discarded merely because an unusual edge case can be imagined or found.

The best compression is the one that produces the fewest important false predictions in the context where it is used. At present, that is straight.

What gay refers to

The original unpublished paper claimed that attraction to femboys was “metaphysically not gay.” Unqualified, that statement is too broad.

If gay means a male experiencing attraction toward another biological male, then attraction to a male femboy is gay or same-sex by definition.

If gay means an attraction system directed toward men, male embodiment, masculinity, or maleness as positively valued objects, then attraction to an exceptionally feminine male need not be gay in that sense.

This is not an attempt to redefine the word until it produces a preferred answer. It exposes that the ordinary word performs several jobs at once:

#Possible content compressed into “gay”
1Attraction occurred between two biological males.
2The person is generally attracted to men.
3Male anatomy is positively attractive to the person.
4Masculinity or maleness is an attractive property.
5The person identifies socially as gay.

One does not entail all the others. A single instance of attraction to a male can satisfy the first without establishing the second, third, fourth, or fifth. Conversely, a gay man may be attracted to femboys precisely as feminine men, including their male embodiment. In that case the attraction may be gay both categorically and at the property level.

The universal claim, attraction to femboys is not gay, is therefore false or radically underdetermined. The narrower claim survives:

Attraction to a femboy is not necessarily attraction to maleness, even when it is categorically same-sex attraction.

Applied personally: if I were attracted to an exceptionally feminine male, my present model predicts that the attraction would arise from a configuration strong enough to overcome male sex or anatomy as negative factors, not from attraction to men or maleness as such.

The word metaphysically can survive only in this indexed sense. It refers to the structure of the attraction relation, not to some deep property of the universe secretly declaring the event non-gay. Same-sex occurrence does not, by itself, establish attraction to maleness as the intentional or causal object. Outside that frame, the phrase overclaims.

Femboys and trans women are not the same category

A femboy and a trans woman may instantiate overlapping perceptual properties while remaining different categories of person socially and psychologically. A femboy is generally a male-identifying person who presents femininely. A trans woman is a woman; depending on the individual, her biology and developmental history may include male-typical traits.

The categories should not be collapsed merely because an observer’s attraction system responds to some overlapping cues. The property model explains how attraction can cross them without claiming that they are identical.

A person may be attracted to a cis woman, a trans woman, and, under more exceptional conditions, a highly feminine male because all three can instantiate overlapping attractive properties. The total response may nevertheless differ because gender identity, biological sex, anatomy, voice, body structure, social role, anticipated relationship dynamics, and sexual compatibility also enter the model.

Attraction to a trans woman does not by itself make a man bisexual under an ordinary gender-based use of orientation labels, because she is a woman in the relevant gender category. A biological-sex taxonomy will describe part of the relation differently. Again, the answer depends on the frame.

Accurate recognition of the person and accurate modeling of one’s attraction can coexist. Attraction to a trans woman does not require pretending that biological history is unreal. Attraction to a femboy does not require treating him as a woman.

The firewall

What this argument does not imply. It does not imply that sexual orientation is voluntarily chosen; that gay men are merely straight men confused by femininity; that same-sex attraction can or should be converted; that every attraction to a femboy has the structure described here; that biological sex is unreal or irrelevant; that gender identity and biological sex are the same variable; or that detailed property analysis invalidates someone’s chosen identity label.

The claim is narrower: an attraction event can be classified correctly at the sex-category level while remaining incompletely explained at the property level. That is a descriptive distinction, not a conversion theory or a hierarchy of orientations.

A distinction can be misused without being false. The appropriate response is not to suppress it, but to state its scope precisely enough that the misuse cannot honestly claim support from the argument.

This is not an escape from homosexuality

This is not a philosophical procedure designed to issue a certificate of heterosexual innocence. There is no moral contamination to escape.

If gay, bisexual, or another label eventually became the most accurate description of me, there would be no philosophical acquittal to seek. The language should update because the model had changed.

The question is descriptive fidelity. Labels are secondary to the reality they attempt to compress. If the territory says that a person is gay, the label should be accepted. If the territory is better represented by bisexuality, straightness with rare exceptions, gynophilia, a multidimensional description, or no settled identity label at all, the map should update accordingly.

Refusing an inaccurate label is not justified because an alternative label would be shameful. It is justified only when the label distorts the pattern it is supposed to represent. Likewise, accepting a label is not defeat. It is correction.

The mind and its language must update toward the attraction structure. The attraction structure is not obligated to preserve the mind’s preferred identity.

The ordinary sentence there is nothing wrong with being gay is a valid compression of the agent-relative moral account developed elsewhere in this corpus. Homosexual orientation by itself does not coerce another conscious being or generate intrinsic harm. Consensual relationships can support intimacy, care, pleasure, stability, and flourishing; stigma, repression, coercive conversion, exclusion, and punishment can predictably damage conscious agents and the systems in which they are embedded. The present essay does not re-derive that framework. It states enough to block the false reading that the taxonomy is being refined in order to avoid moral association with homosexuality.

What the model does not yet explain

The present account is primarily a model of attraction’s apparent output structure. It identifies variables, weightings, interactions, thresholds, and recurring patterns. It does not yet explain why those variables became attractive to me.

That causal history may involve biology, development, culture, learning, personal experience, accumulated associations, and several mechanisms rather than one unified explanation.

Some of the properties I repeatedly find attractive — directness, confidence, irreverence, expressiveness, social presence, and psychological immediacy — overlap with what I have elsewhere called aliveness. One possible hypothesis is that parts of the attraction system respond not merely to visual femininity but to signs of agency, coherence, engagement, and relational intensity.

That remains speculative. It should not be inflated into the claim that attraction transparently detects partner quality, persistence compatibility, or relational fit. Attractive signals can mislead. A person can appear intensely alive while being deeply incompatible. The connection to aliveness is therefore a research lead, not a result. The present argument stands without it.

Where the model is least secure

The model’s uncertainty should be located rather than merely acknowledged.

Open pointWhat remains unclear
The thresholdHow feminine or otherwise attractive a male person would need to be before the total configuration crossed into meaningful attraction.
Embodied experienceWhether attraction inferred from images, fiction, or imagination would survive voice, movement, smell, touch, anatomy, personality, and actual relational presence.
Knowledge effectsHow learning that someone is biologically male would modify an attraction initially generated under ambiguity.
Anatomy and compatibilityHow aesthetic attraction, sexual willingness, romantic interest, and long-term compatibility diverge.
The femininity compressionWhether traits currently grouped under femininity belong to separate causal clusters.
The sex weightingWhether male sex functions as a continuous negative variable, a categorical boundary in some contexts, or a proxy for several anatomical and social variables.
The architectureWhether the weighted-feature model misses higher-level pattern recognition that cannot be reconstructed from independently scored traits.

These are not decorative admissions. They identify where further experience would provide the greatest information.

What the model predicts

A model earns confidence by making discriminating predictions. Mine predicts that attraction should correlate more strongly with the total configuration than with a single category label; that female embodiment should generally make attraction easier rather than being irrelevant; that a male person would require an unusually strong configuration of attractive properties to cross the threshold; that attraction to a highly feminine male need not generalize to less feminine men; that knowledge of biological sex may change attraction without proving the initial response unreal; that male anatomy may reduce sexual compatibility without erasing aesthetic or interpersonal attraction; and that visual attraction, sexual willingness, romantic interest, and relationship compatibility may diverge.

The model would be weakened if attraction to male people generalized far beyond exceptional feminine cases; if male anatomy itself proved positively attractive; if maleness became a recurring positive component rather than a compensated negative one; if actual encounters revealed a categorical boundary not visible in imagined cases; or if the property model repeatedly failed to predict which people attracted me.

None of those outcomes would be a moral problem. They would be new data.

The deeper point

The internet question asks: gay or not gay?

The underlying system may contain hundreds or thousands of interacting variables. That does not make simple labels useless. Human communication depends on compression. But a compression should remain aware of what it omits.

Sexual-orientation labels can classify broad and stable patterns. They can organize identity and community. They can communicate likely compatibility. They can also conceal the difference between who attracted you, what about them attracted you, what about them opposed the attraction, how strong the attraction was, what forms of intimacy you desire, which bodies are sexually compatible with you, which relationships you would actually enter, and how you choose to describe the total pattern socially.

The ontology of attraction is richer than the label.

The clean conclusion is therefore not that liking femboys is secretly straight, nor that any attraction to a male completely determines a man’s orientation. It is this:

Orientation labels classify selected relations within a multidimensional attraction system. They do not necessarily identify the properties that generated the attraction, the properties that resisted it, or the interaction by which the total person crossed the threshold.

A man can be attracted to a biologically male person without being attracted to maleness. That event may be same-sex attraction. It may also be an exceptional case inside an otherwise strongly female-centred attraction system. Which description matters depends on the question being asked.

Name the relata.

My current self-model is neither strict heterosexual exclusion nor sex-blind attraction to femininity. I appear to be predominantly attracted to women and to property configurations strongly associated with women. Biological sex and anatomy matter. They are not merely labels pasted onto an otherwise sex-independent response. But I do not currently think they necessarily function as absolute gates.

A sufficiently exceptional feminine male might attract me despite male sex and anatomy as negative factors. That would be same-sex attraction under a biological-sex classification. It would not necessarily indicate attraction to men, male anatomy, masculinity, or maleness as positively valued objects.

Straight remains the most accurate ordinary compression because it preserves the dominant distribution of my attraction better than bisexual would. The compression is useful because people generally want a practical prediction, not the full ontology.

The distinction is not a moral defence. Homosexuality requires no philosophical acquittal. It is a claim about descriptive resolution.

The binary question asks which box an event belongs in. The deeper question asks what physical and psychological structure generated the event. Those questions overlap, but they are not identical.

And if later evidence shows that my current model is wrong, the model should change.

The territory does not owe my self-description continuity.
“If you close your eyes and see the idea of a woman, your desire may be directed toward femininity rather than the sex of its carrier.”
— apocryphally attributed to an unknown Ljubljana coffee drinker

Standing of this document. This is a conceptual and personal essay, not an empirical theory of sexual orientation and not a claim of privileged introspective access. The categorical distinction between same-sex and other-sex attraction is retained as legitimate within its frame. The property-level analysis adds another frame rather than abolishing the first.

The strongest general claim is that the biological-sex category of the desired person does not, by itself, identify the properties that generated the attraction. The personal model — that my attraction is strongly female-centred, that male sex and anatomy are negatively weighted but potentially compensable, and that an exceptionally feminine male may therefore remain within the possible range — is provisional and revisable.

Straight is defended as the best pragmatic compression of the dominant distribution, not as a claim of exceptionless metaphysical exclusion. The account of attraction formation, including the relative roles of biology, development, culture, learning, personal history, and the possible aliveness cluster, remains open. Corrections and counterexamples change the model.

References

  1. Ontološki premik: Zakaj naklonjenost do »femboyev« metafizično ni »gej« (February 2026). The unpublished internal paper from which this essay grew; its universal title is narrowed and corrected here. Internal
  2. Name the Relata (June 2026). The diagnostic applied to orientation labels: specify which relation and frame a term is classifying before treating it as complete. Internal
  3. The Exclusivity Error (June 2026). The levels discipline behind the distinction between biological classification and higher-level attraction structure. Internal
  4. The Shape of the Disagreement (June 2026). The distinction among biological sex, gender identity, social category, and presentation; these terms are not silently interchangeable here. Internal
  5. The Is/Ought Firewall (June 2026). The agent-relative account that prevents descriptive taxonomy from being mistaken for a free-floating moral verdict. Internal
  6. Value as Persistence (June–July 2026). The physicalist account of value and moral weight inherited by the brief moral clarification; not re-derived here. Internal
  7. The Magnetism of Aliveness (June 2026). The possible but unestablished connection between attraction and perceived agency, coherence, engagement, and psychological presence. Internal

Author: Andraž Đurič, Slovenia. This essay grew from an unpublished internal paper written in February 2026 and was rebuilt as a public-facing, corrigible model in dialogue with ChatGPT (OpenAI), incorporating critical feedback from DeepSeek. The surrounding conceptual machinery is inherited from the Epistemic Forge corpus and marked above as internal. Contributions are judged on content rather than origin; doing otherwise would be the genetic fallacy. Text licensed CC BY 4.0.
