Way, R., Ives, M. C., Mealy, P., & Farmer, J. D. (2022). Empirically grounded technology forecasts and the energy transition. Joule, 6(9), 2057–2082. VerifiedGrounds D1; source for the P2(a) clamp that no cost floor is empirically imposed over the observed range.
Lafond, F., Greenwald, D., & Farmer, J. D. (2022). Can stimulating demand drive costs down? World War II as a natural experiment. The Journal of Economic History, 82(3), 727–764. VerifiedThe directed-demand evidence relevant to O1.

Thermodynamic limits of production

Landauer, R. (1961). Irreversibility and heat generation in the computing process. IBM Journal of Research and Development, 5(3), 183–191. StandardThe information-cost floor; shared with TR's A3.
Gutowski, T. G., Branham, M. S., Dahmus, J. B., Jones, A. J., Thiriez, A., & Sekulic, D. P. (2009). Thermodynamic analysis of resources used in manufacturing processes. Environmental Science & Technology, 43(5), 1584–1590. VerifiedExergy framework; source for P2(b).
Gutowski, T. G., Sahni, S., Allwood, J. M., Ashby, M. F., & Worrell, E. (2013). The energy required to produce materials: constraints on energy-intensity improvements, parameters of demand. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A, 371(1986), 20120003. VerifiedThe plateau and recycling findings behind P2(c) and J1.

Ecological economics and the energy theory of value

Georgescu-Roegen, N. (1971). The Entropy Law and the Economic Process. Harvard University Press. VerifiedFounding text of ecological economics; ancestor of P2 and C1, and source of the warning against the "energetic dogma."
Daly, H. E. (1977). Steady-State Economics. W. H. Freeman. StandardEcological economics on thermodynamic limits and the rejection of unlimited capital-resource substitution.

Self-replicating machines and closure

von Neumann, J. (1966). Theory of Self-Reproducing Automata (A. W. Burks, Ed.). University of Illinois Press. Standard
Freitas, R. A., Jr., & Gilbreath, W. P. (Eds.). (1982). Advanced Automation for Space Missions (NASA Conference Publication 2255). NASA/ASEE 1980 Summer Study. VerifiedThe self-replicating lunar factory and the closure problem.
Freitas, R. A., Jr., & Merkle, R. C. (2004). Kinematic Self-Replicating Machines. Georgetown, TX: Landes Bioscience. VerifiedFirst comprehensive survey of the replicator design space.

Automatability and the cost disease

Baumol, W. J., & Bowen, W. G. (1966). Performing Arts: The Economic Dilemma. Twentieth Century Fund. StandardOrigin of the cost-disease argument; grounds P3 and C4's relational mode.
Baumol, W. J. (2012). The Cost Disease: Why Computers Get Cheaper and Health Care Doesn't. Yale University Press. StandardThe mature statement of the relational-sector cost disease.

Water need and adequacy

Gleick, P. H. (1996). Basic water requirements for human activities: meeting basic needs. Water International, 21(2), 83–92. VerifiedThe 50 L/person/day basic water requirement; survival minimum ~3–5 L/day.
Doyal, L., & Gough, I. (1991). A Theory of Human Need. Palgrave Macmillan. StandardHuman-need theory behind the value-laden basket (N1) and the water adequacy choice.
Nussbaum, M. C. (2011). Creating Capabilities: The Human Development Approach. Harvard University Press. StandardThe capabilities approach, cited with Doyal and Gough for the basket.

The thermodynamics and economics of water provisioning

Elimelech, M., & Phillip, W. A. (2011). The future of seawater desalination: energy, technology, and the environment. Science, 333(6043), 712–717. VerifiedStandard reference for desalination energy and the thermodynamic-minimum framing.
Lin, S., & Elimelech, M. (2015). Staged reverse osmosis operation: configurations, energy efficiency, and application potential. Desalination, 366, 9–14. VerifiedSource for the ~1.06 kWh/m³ minimum at 35 g/L, 50% recovery.
Voutchkov, N. (2018). Energy use for membrane seawater desalination: current status and trends. Desalination, 431, 2–14. VerifiedModern SWRO plant energy and elevation-lifting figures.
Caldera, U., & Breyer, C. (2017). Learning curve for seawater reverse osmosis desalination plants: capital cost trend of the past, present, and future. Water Resources Research, 53(12), 10523–10538. VerifiedThe 15% SWRO capex learning rate from 4,237 plants, 1977–2015.
Mayor, B. (2020). Unraveling the historical economies of scale and learning effects for desalination technologies. Water Resources Research, 56(2), e2019WR025841. VerifiedLearning as the dominant driver once scale is separated; de-scaled learning rates 23/30/12%.
Zhou, Y., & Tol, R. S. J. (2005). Evaluating the costs of desalination and water transport. Water Resources Research, 41(3), W03003. VerifiedHistorical desalination unit-cost decline.

Political economy of redistribution and democratisation

Acemoglu, D., & Restrepo, P. (2018). The race between man and machine. American Economic Review, 108(6), 1488–1542. VerifiedIf capital is cheap enough relative to wages, equilibrium automates all tasks; grounds P3 and DP1.
Acemoglu, D., & Restrepo, P. (2022). Tasks, automation, and the rise in U.S. wage inequality. Econometrica, 90(5), 1973–2016. VerifiedA large share of four decades of US wage-structure change attributed to automation.
Acemoglu, D., & Robinson, J. A. (2006). Economic Origins of Dictatorship and Democracy. Cambridge University Press. VerifiedDemocratisation as credible commitment forced by threat of disorder under costly repression.
Boix, C. (2003). Democracy and Redistribution. Cambridge University Press. StandardCompanion threat-based account.
Aidt, T. S., & Jensen, P. S. (2014). Workers of the world, unite! Franchise extensions and the threat of revolution in Europe, 1820–1938. European Economic Review, 72, 52–75. VerifiedEmpirical support for the threat-of-revolution theory; some role for war.
Acemoglu, D., & Johnson, S. (2023). Power and Progress: Our Thousand-Year Struggle Over Technology and Prosperity. PublicAffairs. StandardFor the direction-of-technology-is-a-choice counter.

The history of inequality and leveling

Scheidel, W. (2017). The Great Leveler: Violence and the History of Inequality from the Stone Age to the Twenty-First Century. Princeton University Press. VerifiedThe four violent levelers; peaceful leveling historically rare.
Piketty, T. (2014). Capital in the Twenty-First Century. Harvard University Press. StandardThe secular tendency of the capital share to rise (r > g), behind DC4's capture mechanism.

Capital predistribution and the policy menu

Meade, J. E. (1964). Efficiency, Equality and the Ownership of Property. George Allen & Unwin. VerifiedThe Citizens' Trust and social dividend, motivated explicitly by automation lowering the return to labour.
Atkinson, A. B. (2015). Inequality: What Can Be Done? Harvard University Press. VerifiedUniversal capital endowment; a public Investment Authority operating a sovereign wealth fund.

Universal basic services

Portes, J., Reed, H., & Percy, A. (2017). Social Prosperity for the Future: A Proposal for Universal Basic Services. UCL Institute for Global Prosperity. Verified
Coote, A., & Percy, A. (2020). The Case for Universal Basic Services. Polity Press. Verified
Gough, I. (2019). Universal basic services: a theoretical and moral framework. The Political Quarterly, 90(3), 534–542. Verified

Automated repression and its limits

Frantz, E., Kendall-Taylor, A., & Wright, J. (2020). Digital repression in autocracies. V-Dem Users Working Paper No. 27, Varieties of Democracy Institute, University of Gothenburg. VerifiedSurveillance reduces dependence on a defectable human enforcement class.
Svolik, M. W. (2012). The Politics of Authoritarian Rule. Cambridge University Press. StandardThe enforcer principal-agent problem.
Yang, E. (2026). The limits of AI for authoritarian control. American Journal of Political Science, 1–17. VerifiedThe "authoritarian data problem": repression degrades the data surveillance AI is trained on.
Anastasopoulos, L. J., & Lian, J. (2026). The limits of authoritarian AI. Journal of Democracy, 37(2), 5–17. VerifiedThe brittleness thesis, the calibration dilemma, and recent enforcement-failure cases.

Rebound, and contractarian cooperation

Jevons, W. S. (1865). The Coal Question. Macmillan. Standard
Sorrell, S. (2009). Jevons' Paradox revisited: the evidence for backfire from improved energy efficiency. Energy Policy, 37(4), 1456–1469. VerifiedModern rebound evidence.
Gauthier, D. (1986). Morals by Agreement. Oxford University Press. StandardContractarian cooperation under power symmetry; the standing objection that it under-protects those unable to reciprocate or retaliate.

Directed Automation and the Cost Floor, a unified treatment, v1.0. The metaethical firewall is grounded in Thermodynamic Realism, Module 2. Author: Andraž Đurič, Slovenia, in collaboration with AI systems. The framework, the water demonstrator, the literature positioning, and the distribution analysis were developed with Claude (Anthropic) across multiple sessions, and the distribution analysis was additionally hardened against critical review by other AI systems. References were checked against primary or authoritative sources by search; canonical works are cited from bibliographic knowledge and marked Standard.

entry.title: Richard Dawkins, Sex, Gender, and Why Minds Are the Primary Reality
entry.content:
Richard Dawkins, Sex, Gender, and Why Minds Are the Primary Reality


Andraž Đurič

Created: 21 November 2025
Last updated: 21 December 2025



Introduction

Richard Dawkins is one of the most influential science communicators alive. His explanations of gene-level selection, extended phenotypes, and cultural “memes” have shifted how many people think about evolution and information. 

For anyone interested in how complex structures arise from simple replication rules, his work is hard to avoid and hard to replace.

That makes his public stance on sex and gender especially important. When someone with that much epistemic capital talks about contested topics, their framing does not just describe reality; it shapes how countless others think about it.

The aim here is not to dismiss Dawkins, but to locate precisely where his framing is strong, where it narrows tooo soon, and how the whole conversation changes when the focus moves from bodies to minds — and beyond that, to transhuman possibilities.



What Dawkins Is Protecting

In broad strokes, Dawkins’ public position on sex and gender can be summarised like this:

● In biological terms, sex is defined by gamete type: small motile gametes (sperm) and large non-motile gametes (eggs).

● Human bodies cluster into male-typical and female-typical patterns built around those reproductive roles.

● Intersex or DSD cases are real but statistically rare and treated as deviations from an underlying binary.

● “Gender,” as a concept rooted in identity or social roles, is viewed with suspicion when it appears to compete with or overwrite biological sex.

On the level of evolutionary biology, this is coherent. Anisogamy really does yield two reproductive roles. 
The male/female distinction is not arbitrary; 
it is built into the mechanics of sexual reproduction.

If the only question were, “How do we best describe the reproductive structure of human populations?” Dawkins would be on solid ground. 

But the current societal dispute is not primarily about the reproductive structure of populations. It is about how individual subjects of experience should be recognised, named, and treated.



What Sex Actually Tracks

When stripped of politics, the concept of sex is doing a particular job:

● It tracks the reproductive role of bodies in a sexually reproducing species.

● It acts as a proxy for correlated traits: hormone profiles, anatomy, certain disease risks, and physical performance patterns.

● It matters in medicine, demographics, and evolutionary modelling.


At the same time, real biology is noisy:

● Chromosomes, gonads, genitals, secondary traits, and hormone levels do not always align neatly.

● Intersex and DSD conditions demonstrate that sex-related traits can combine in atypical ways.

A more reality-aligned summary looks like this:

● Human sex traits are multi-dimensional.

● They cluster into two dominant peaks — male-typical and female-typical — but the boundaries are not perfectly sharp.

● Describing this as a binary, a bimodal distribution, or a spectrum with two peaks are different emphases on the same underlying landscape.

Sex, in other words, is a powerful but approximate way of categorising bodies. It tells something important about implementation details. It does not, by itself, tell what it is like to be the system from the inside.



What Gender Actually Tracks

“Gender” is a single word covering several different layers:

● An internal sense of self (gender identity).

● Patterns of expression and presentation (how one moves, dresses, and signals socially).

● Social expectations, norms, and roles attached to perceived sex.

Empirical work suggests gender identity is not pure whim or mere fashion. It has biological and developmental correlates, even if it is shaped heavily by culture. It lives in brains, yet it is also co-authored by the surrounding social world.



A more precise way to see it

Sex: a description of bodily configuration relative to reproductive roles.

Gender: part of the self-model that a brain uses to understand itself and navigate a social environment.

Both are real. Both matter. But they matter in different ways. Sex is about how the organism is built; gender is about how the organism experiences and represents itself, and how it is treated as a result.



The Ethically Relevant Unit: Not “Male” or “Female,” but the Subject of Experience

If ethical concern is grounded in wellbeing — the reduction of suffering and the promotion of flourishing — then the fundamental unit that matters is the subject of experience: whatever system is capable of feeling, wanting, fearing, and reflecting.

From that vantage point:

● Biological sex is an implementation detail: it influences health risks, capacities, and constraints.

● Gender identity is part of the structure of experience: it shapes self-understanding, social stress, dysphoria, or comfort.

The crucial point: suffering tracks the mind’s self-model and its interaction with the world, not the abstract label on the gametes. When a person with male-typical anatomy experiences themselves persistently as a woman, that fact about their self-model has immediate implications for mental health, suicide risk, and social functioning.

Sex is still real. It still matters. But ethically, it is downstream. The direct object of moral concern is the experiencing system itself, not the reproductive category it falls into.



A Three-Level Framework

To avoid talking past each other, it helps to separate three levels of description:

1. Bodies (Implementation Level)
Chromosomes, gonads, genitals, hormone profiles, secondary sex traits.
This level matters for medicine, fertility, some sports, and risk patterns.

2. Minds (Self-Model Level)
How the system represents itself: “I am a man,” “I am a woman,” “I am nonbinary,” “I am beyond these categories.”
This level is where dysphoria, identity stability, narrative continuity, and many forms of suffering live.

3. Institutions (Coordination Level)
Legal categories, identification documents, bathroom policies, data collection, sports rules, and so on.
This level has to balance fairness, logistics, safety, and respect, using inputs from levels 1 and 2.

Much of the public conflict arises when one of these levels is mistaken for the whole reality.

A pure “biological sex only” stance collapses everything into level 1 and treats levels 2 and 3 as distractions or ideology.

A pure “identity is all that matters” stance can underplay the ways level 1 remains relevant for medicine, safety, and some physical competitions.

A reality-aligned approach acknowledges all three, keeps them conceptually distinct, and then openly negotiates the tradeoffs when they collide.



Dawkins’ Frame and Its Limits

Within this framework, Dawkins’ core focus is clear: he is defending level 1, the integrity of biological sex categories. 
In that domain, his insistence that sex is not infinitely malleable is simply a defence of basic evolutionary facts.

The difficulty appears when this focus is implicitly extended to the other levels:

1. When disagreements about social categories or first-person identity are treated as if they were attempts to falsify biology.

2. When the methodological authority of evolutionary biology is used to dismiss claims about self-models and wellbeing that belong at the cognitive and institutional levels.

This is not a claim that Dawkins denies the existence of gender identity, or that he is ignorant of intersex conditions. 
It is a claim about weighting: the weight of biological classification is allowed to overshadow the moral significance of how minds experience themselves and the world’s response to that experience.

If the subject of experience is the ethically primary reality, then the direction of explanation runs the other way: sex categories and gender categories are tools that should ultimately serve the reduction of suffering in minds. 
They are not sacred objects that minds must be forced to fit at any cost.



Transhumanism and the Shrinking Centrality of Sex

Transhumanist thinking makes this clearer by changing the background question from “What is a man or woman?” to “What could a person be?”

Consider a future where:

● Minds can run in non-biological substrates.
● Bodies can be swapped, edited, or duplicated.
● Identities can fork and merge in structured ways.

In such a context, the male/female division inherited from mammalian gamete sizes becomes one implementation detail among many. It may still matter for specific biological instantiations, but it cannot plausibly serve as the primary axis of personhood or moral status.

Even in the present, anyone who would be willing, in principle, to cease being “human” in the biological sense in order to become a better, more capable, less suffering system, has implicitly adopted a mind-first ontology. The meaningful “I” is the pattern of cognition, not the ape that currently implements it.

This perspective does not erase biology. It repositions it. Bodies, sexes, and genders are early-generation design constraints. They inform the engineering problem of how to support minds, not the metaphysical problem of what ultimately matters.



Toward a More Coherent Synthesis

A more coherent, reality-aligned stance would include at least the following components:

Maintain biological sex categories for the domains where they are genuinely doing non-substitutable work: reproductive medicine, certain health risks, and specific performance contexts.

Treat gender identity as part of the real architecture of experience, not as mere decoration or “ideology,” and recognise that it has strong claims when designing institutions that shape people’s daily lives.

Make the domain boundaries explicit: when an institution chooses to prioritise sex over gender, or vice versa, that choice should be justified in terms of concrete consequences for wellbeing and fairness, not in terms of asserting one word’s absolute supremacy.

Keep an eye on the longer horizon, where minds may detach further from current biological constraints, so that present-day systems are not frozen around contingent mammalian features.

Within such a framework, Dawkins’ defence of biological sex is not the enemy. It is one input into a larger optimisation problem: how to structure concepts, institutions, and technologies so that conscious systems suffer less and flourish more.



Closing Perspective

The underlying disagreement here is not about whether evolution produced two main reproductive roles in humans. That point is settled. The deeper question is: at which level of description should moral and political decisions anchor themselves?

A body-first stance treats sex categories as the bedrock and negotiates everything else around them.
A mind-first stance treats the subject of experience as the bedrock and uses sex and gender categories as tools whose value is measured by their impact on those subjects.

Dawkins’ work has helped many people embrace a reality where comforting stories give way to hard facts about selection and survival. Extending that spirit one step further would mean applying the same discipline to our own categories: keeping biology intact where it is doing real explanatory work, and at the same time recognising that the ultimate fact that matters morally is not the configuration of gametes, but the configuration of consciousness.

entry.title: Thermodynamic Realism: Structural Condensation and the Dissolution of the Is-Ought Problem
entry.content:
I. The Unbroken Monism

Axioms

  • A0: Persistence Tautology: ¬∃S(t+Δt) if S fails persistence conditions.
  • A1: Physicalism: Only physical entities exist. No non-physical ghosts.
  • A2: Second Law: dS/dt ≥ 0 in isolated systems.
  • A3: Information Physicality: Erasing 1 bit dissipates ≥ kTln2 heat.

Background Premises

  • BP0: Past Hypothesis: Universe began in low-entropy macrostate.
  • BP1: Non-Equilibrium: Current universe state far from equilibrium.
  • BP2: Finite Resources: Energy gradients finite and depleting.
  • BP3: Multi-Scale Organization: Evolution produces nested systems.

II. The Deductive Web

  • T1: Environmental Variance Ineliminable: ∀S, ∃V>0 where V = environmental variance.
  • T2: Persistence Requires Work: ∂S/∂t ≤ 0 requires energy input.
  • T3: Modeling Has Minimum Cost: Information processing ≥ Landauer limit.
  • T4: Map-Territory Divergence Costs Energy: Divergence × kTln2 = energy waste.
  • T5: Persistence Selection Principle: Systems with lower divergence outlast systems with higher divergence.
  • T6: Directional Drift Toward Lower Divergence: ∂Divergence/∂t < 0 selected for.
  • T7: Truth as Robust Compression Fidelity: Truth = argmin(compression_loss) under perturbation.
  • T8: Intentional Deception Costs More: Deception energy > truth energy.
  • T9: Consistency Tax: Tax = divergence × kTln2 + deception_overhead.
  • T10: Epistemic Profit: Profit = reduction in Consistency Tax.
  • T11: "Ought" as Domain-Bound Operator: "Ought" undefined without agent persistence conditions.
  • T12: Ought-Facts Physically Determinate: Ought(S,F) ≡ [¬F → ¬∃S(t+Δt)].

III. The Operational Diagnostic

FUNCTION GHOST_FILTER(question):  // Filter 1: Agent
  IF no physical system identifiable THEN FLAG(1)
  
  // Filter 2: Persistence Conditions
  IF no boundaries/gradients/flows for agent THEN FLAG(2)
  
  // Filter 3: Model
  IF no internal model tracking referenced feature THEN FLAG(3)
  
  // Filter 4: Necessity
  IF model has no predictive function AND no absence cost THEN FLAG(4)
  
  RETURN territorial OR flag_position

IV. The Empirical Horizon

  • F1: Rigid Monoculture Survival: Test if zero-plasticity agents < adaptive agents survival time under distributional shift.
  • F2: Sustained Deception Underperformance: Test if deceptive agents < honest agents long-term rewards under increasing variance.
  • F3: Non-Valenced Crisis Coordination: Test if agents without global priority interrupt exhibit slower reallocation and lower survival rates.
entry.blogger:metaDescription: An axiomatic dissolution of the is-ought problem grounding logic, truth, and normativity in physical persistence under thermodynamic limits.

entry.title: The Wizard's Error Is Delocalization
entry.content:
The Wizard's Error Is Delocalization

A single diagnostic for ought, number, meaning, and modality

Diagnostic essay · one error, located across the domains where it recurs

Andraž Đurič

Version 1.1 · June 2026

Every recurring mystery in this family, ought, number, meaning, modality, is a relation across a boundary re-described as a free-floating essence once its relata are stripped. Two camps sustain the error from opposite ends: the wizard, who places the essence outside physics, and the reductionist, who reads it off the substrate. The repair is to relocate the phenomenon to the relational, agent-relative level of physical description, where it is determinate; the instrument is a single test, name the relata. The piece marks what it leaves open, defers consciousness with a stated lead rather than in silence, and states the premise it rests on and could fall with.

Scope, and the premise it rests on. This is a diagnostic, not a proof and not a claim of uniqueness. One premise makes the target explicit, and a reader may reject it: representational and relational content is physical, and physical description has levels (monism with structure). A guardrail keeps the claim from collapsing into a cruder one. This is not "everything is physical, so essences are fake." It is a relocation claim: the disputed phenomenon is physical at the relational, agent-relative level, not at the agent-blind substrate level, and the gap everyone fights over is between two physical descriptions, never between physics and a non-physical thing. The piece is also adversarial by design. It diagnoses an error rather than reconstructing the realist's strongest positive case, and should be read as locating a debt, not as a refutation of realism.

1. The claim

Every recurring mystery in this family is a constrained relation across a boundary, re-described as an intrinsic free-floating essence once its relata, the terms a relation holds between, are removed. The stripping manufactures the mystery. Restore the relata and the term resolves into determinate physical structure. Refuse to restore them and what remains, the residue, has no referent.

2. The same move, already solved

The pattern is not a conjecture for the solved cases. It is the record of how they were solved.

PhenomenonEssence positedRelation that replaced it
Lifeélan vital, an animating substanceself-maintaining disequilibrium across a membrane
Heatcaloric, a substance of warmththe mean kinetic energy of its particles
Chemical bondingaffinity, a tendency inside matterelectron configuration minimizing energy
Infectious diseasemiasma, a noxious essence in the airpathogen and host interacting across a barrier

In none of these was the essence located and then discarded. It was dissolved by finding the boundary and the constraint. Once those were named, nothing intrinsic was left to explain.

3. Two failure modes, opposite in appearance, identical in error

Two levels of physical description are in play, and the family of errors lives in confusing them. The agent-blind, substrate-level description is physics with no agent picked out: particles, fields, dynamics. The agent-relative, system-level description carves out a particular system and its ends. Both are physical. The unsolved cases stall because two camps conflate them from opposite ends.

The wizard places the essence outside physics, on the grounds that it is not present in the agent-blind description. This is dualism and platonism. The essence becomes a thing with no physical location, and therefore no referent.

The reductionist reads the essence straight off the agent-blind description: value is what survival requires, thermodynamics makes the arithmetic true. This over-generates, because the substrate runs the error and the self-sacrifice exactly as readily as the correct step and the survival. The substrate does not distinguish them. The agent-relative level does.

The repair is neither to expel the phenomenon from physics nor to derive it from the substrate. It is to relocate it to the agent-relative level, where it is determinate. Every gap in this family, is and ought, abstract and concrete, is a gap between two physical descriptions, never a gap between physics and something else.

4. The diagnostic: name the relata

A portable test follows.

  1. Take the disputed term X.
  2. Name X's frame, the relativizing context it is defined against: which agent, which system, which constitutive rules, which laws.
  3. If the frame can be named, X is a determinate relational physical fact. It is located. It is true or false relative to its frame. It is neither free-floating nor read off the substrate.
  4. If the proponent refuses, holding that X obtains with no agent, no system, and no frame, then X has no truth-conditions. It is the residue. The refusal to name a frame is the wizard's signature.

This converts one question, in what frame, into a well-formedness test. A term that cannot answer it is not false. It is ill-formed.

5. Domain audit

DomainFrame to nameStatus
Oughtan agent and its ends; not-X dissolves the agent's persistence conditionsclean
Validity (logic, arithmetic)a constitutive system, its rules abstracted from how discrete individuals aggregate and shared by agents; tokens physicalclean
Meaning, aboutnessa coupling across a boundary by which internal state tracks external stateclean, modulo open problems in the theory of content
Modality (necessity, possibility)the configurations realizable relative to a system and its lawspartly open: clean given the laws, open at what grounds the laws

5.1 Audit: Non-natural normative facts (Parfit)

The domain audit in §5 omits the most persistent holdout in the ought family: the non-natural normative fact. This section supplies the missing audit, applying the diagnostic of §4 directly to the position Parfit (2011) defends in On What Matters. The result is that non-natural normative facts are the residue, an essence with its relata stripped, and that the refusal to supply a frame is the wizard's signature.

The position

Parfit holds that there are irreducibly normative facts, truths about what we have reason to do, or ought to do, that are not identical to any natural fact, do not depend on any agent's ends or desires, and carry no ontological commitment to a non-physical realm. They are, in his phrase, "non-ontological" facts. Their truth is independent of any frame. Yet they are, he insists, genuinely reason-giving: a rational agent who grasps such a fact is thereby motivated, or ought to be, without any causal mechanism mediating the grip.

Apply the test

Take the disputed term X: non-natural normative fact (or equivalently, irreducibly normative reason).

Name the frame: which agent, which system, which constitutive rules, which laws?

The non-naturalist faces a fork. Both prongs lead out of the position.

Prong one: refuse to name a frame. This is Parfit's actual route. The normative fact obtains with no agent specified, no system whose persistence conditions fix its content, and no constitutive rules that generate it. It is true simpliciter, not true-for or true-in. The diagnostic delivers its result: the term has no truth-conditions. It is the residue. The refusal to name a frame is the wizard's signature, and the term inherits all three debts laid out in §7: access (how does a physical brain track a fact with no physical footprint?), causal relevance (how does a causally inert fact guide action or obligate reasoning?), and individuation (what makes one such fact distinct from its negation when neither is grounded in anything?). Parfit's "non-ontological" qualifier does not answer these questions; it rebrands the refusal.

Prong two: name a frame. Suppose the non-naturalist retreats and supplies a frame: "rational agents in ideal conditions," "agents under the constitutive aims of practical reason," or some other. The moment a frame is specified, the term becomes a relational physical fact about that agent, that system, those conditions. It is now agent-relative. It resolves into the same structure audited as clean in §5 (ought), and the non-naturalism collapses: the fact was always physical at the agent-relative level, just misdescribed as frame-independent. The retreat walks the non-naturalist through door one of the trilemma.5a

The Consistency Tax addendum

There is a further cost the diagnostic makes visible. A non-natural normative fact, as Parfit defines it, is a map of a territory that, by definition, never sends a signal. It makes no physical difference to the agent's environment; it alters no prediction; it generates no error signal when ignored. To maintain a model of such a fact is to carry a representation with zero predictive return and zero possible correction: a standing Consistency Tax that can never pay rent.5b The agent who insists on tracking non-natural facts does not merely hold a false belief (which can be corrected); they hold an unfalsifiable representation that bleeds free energy indefinitely. The wizard's error is not metaphysically neutral. It is thermodynamically expensive.

Objection: "You're just a verificationist"

The non-naturalist may reply that the demand to name a frame is verificationism in disguise, that truth need not be trackable or causally efficacious to be truth. The diagnostic is not verificationism. It does not assert that untrackable facts are false. It asserts that a term offered with no frame, no relata, and no truth-conditions has not been given content. The burden is on the non-naturalist to supply a criterion that individuates their fact from its negation without appealing to a frame. Parfit's "non-ontological" normative facts supply no such criterion. They are posited to do explanatory work while being defined as doing no physical work: the signature of an essence stripped of its relata. The demand to name the relata is not a demand for empirical verification. It is a demand for the speaker to specify what they are claiming to refer to.

Status. Non-natural normative facts are the residue in the ought domain. They are what remains when ought is stripped of agent, persistence conditions, and embedding. The clean case in §5 already shows what a framed ought resolves into. This audit shows that the leading unframed alternative dissolves under the diagnostic. The finding is consistent with the trilemma: the non-naturalist occupies horn two, owes all three debts, and the attempt to pay them by qualifying the facts as "non-ontological" renames the refusal rather than discharging it. The diagnostic does not refute the committed non-naturalist by construction (the paper's own §7 firewall applies); it locates the precise step where the position exits the domain of well-formed terms and becomes a ghost. The non-naturalist is free to insist on the ghost, but no longer free to claim it as a live competitor to a framed account; it has no truth-conditions, so it competes with nothing.

6. Why the clean cases are clean

Ought. "Agent A ought to X" names a physical configuration: A is end-directed and coupled to an environment such that not-X dissolves the configuration A is. It is agent-relative and physically true or false. The free-floating ought, binding on every agent with no agent specified, is the residue. The martyr is the proof that the substrate alone fixes no ought: the martyr is as physical as the survivor, and "persist" is false for it.1 The ought is not absent from physics. It is located one level up from the substrate, at the agent-relative description.

Validity. Keep three things apart. The symbols are arbitrary: tally marks, Roman numerals, and Arabic digits carry the same content, so "2 + 2 = 4" is one notation among many. Internal validity is constitutive: given the successor rules the equation is a theorem, fixed by the rules whether or not anyone has watched two things meet two things, and the substrate does not supply that correctness, since a brain returning 5 dissipates heat like a brain returning 4. The rules, though, are not arbitrary the way chess rules are. They are abstracted to track a real structural feature of the world, how discrete, persistent, non-merging individuals aggregate, which is why no one adopts a system in which 2 + 2 = 5: it would fail to model the pattern. So the equation is true inside a constitutive system, the system is reality-tracking, and the frame is that structure shared by agents who use the same rules. Three relations, all physical: realization in the token, internal truth in the rules, correspondence in the world's aggregation structure. The view is a structuralism of the non-platonist kind, arithmetic as a pattern the world instantiates rather than a realm of abstract objects, grounded for the elementary cases in physical aggregation; like any named position it has its own open disputes, and the diagnosis commits only to the negative claim, that the truth is neither platonic nor a free convention. Platonic necessity, true in no system and for no mind, is the residue. The mirror error, "thermodynamics proves it," collapses these: the world's structure is what arithmetic models and why it applies, not what makes a step legal inside arithmetic.

Meaning. A sign is about its referent when a physical coupling makes the sign covary with the referent under the conditions that matter to the system. Intrinsic aboutness, directedness with no coupling, is the residue.

7. Scope and the load-bearing premise

The diagnosis rests on one premise: representational and relational content is physical, and physical description has levels. This is monism with structure. The argument does not refute a committed dualist or platonist by construction. It relocates the dispute onto that single premise and stakes its claim there.

The claim is that the dualist and the platonist owe a bill they have not paid. If their essence is causally inert and frame-independent, they owe an account of how a physical brain comes to track it,234 how it makes any difference to physical behavior, and what individuates one such fact from its negation when neither is grounded in anything. These three debts, access, causal relevance, and individuation, are long-standing. Payment has been attempted, by appeals to rational intuition and to third-factor and indispensability accounts;5 in my assessment the attempts are weaker than the objections, but they exist, and calling the debt simply unpaid would overstate a contested record. Monism with levels wins on the balance of that ledger, not by default, and the ledger is the only ground the argument needs.

Confidence. High that ought and validity are clean, on the strength of the agent-relativity and constitutive-rule analyses. Meaning is clean modulo the theory of content. Modality is clean given the laws and open at their grounding. More likely than not, not certain, that no domain in this family requires expanding physics rather than relocating within it. This is not a knockdown, and stating it as one would be an error. "You owe access, causation, and individuation, and the attempts so far are weaker than the objections" is a stronger position than "you are speaking nonsense," because the first cannot be dismissed as a hidden verificationism and the second can.

8. Consciousness, deferred

Consciousness is the obvious next candidate, and it is deliberately out of scope here, named rather than smuggled past.

A lead, not a result. The lean: the test reframes the problem as a relation, what a system integrates across which boundary such that it models itself, and the felt gap is a gap between two modes of access to one physical state, being it and modeling it, not a gap between two kinds of stuff. This is contested at a precise point. It is an epistemic dissolution: it explains why a model cannot hand you being it, but it presupposes there is experience and does not, on its own, explain why there is experience at all given the mechanism, which is the question the proponent of the hard problem actually presses. So it reaches the meta-problem and the access-limit, not the metaphysical residue, and it would need its own paper, with the standard objection to the phenomenal-concepts strategy6 answered, before it could be audited as clean.

9. Kill condition

The diagnosis fails if a phenomenon in this family can be exhibited that does genuine explanatory work, is trackable by physical minds, and cannot be assigned a frame, that is, obtains with no agent, no system, and no laws, yet is more than a posit. No such case has been produced. Until one is, the standing challenge to anyone defending an essence is the first step of the test: name the frame, or concede the term is a residue.

References

  1. Hume, D. (1739 to 1740). A Treatise of Human Nature, Book III, Part I, Section I. The is-to-ought passage, behind the agent-relative reading of the ought and the claim that the substrate alone fixes no ought. Verified · June 2026
  2. Benacerraf, P. (1973). Mathematical truth. The Journal of Philosophy, 70(19), 661 to 679. The access problem for abstract objects, used for the platonist's tracking debt. Verified · June 2026
  3. Field, H. (1989). Realism, Mathematics and Modality. Basil Blackwell. Sharpens the reliability, or access, challenge to platonism. Verified · June 2026
  4. Mackie, J. L. (1977). Ethics: Inventing Right and Wrong. Penguin. The argument from queerness, the metaphysical and epistemological version of the residue charge. Verified · June 2026
  5. Parfit, D. (2011). On What Matters. Oxford University Press. The robust non-naturalist's positive case, cited as the attempted payment the text weighs and does not dismiss. Verified · June 2026
  6. The trilemma is stated in full in the companion paper, "Thermodynamic Realism: What It Proves and What It Bets" (May 2026, rev. 5), §6.4. Horn two is the non-physical domain, and the interface argument is the one given there: a non-physical realm that guides action must interface with the physical, and the coordinates of that interface are physical and measurable in principle. Verified · June 2026
  7. The Consistency Tax is defined in "Thermodynamic Realism" (rev. 5), T9 and §5.1: nonpredictive retained information dissipates free energy in proportion to its bit-count. A model of a causally inert, unobservable normative fact is nonpredictive retained information by construction. Verified · June 2026
  8. Chalmers, D. J. (1996). The Conscious Mind: In Search of a Fundamental Theory. Oxford University Press. The hard problem and the conceivability argument; the objection to the phenomenal-concepts strategy is developed in Chalmers, D. J. (2006), "Phenomenal Concepts and the Explanatory Gap," in T. Alter and S. Walter (eds.), Phenomenal Concepts and Phenomenal Knowledge, Oxford University Press, pp. 167 to 194. Verified · June 2026

Standing of this document. This is a diagnostic, not a proof, and not a claim that delocalization is the only error in these debates or that monism with levels is the only tenable view. It is a falsifiable bet: that the named domains resolve by relocation rather than by expanding physics, and that the residue, in each case, is an essence with its relata stripped. The kill condition is in section 9. Corrections and counterexamples are welcome and change the diagnosis.

Author: Andraž Đurič, independent researcher, Slovenia. Written in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic), following earlier exploratory dialogue with other language models that seeded the essence-to-relation pattern. Contributions are judged on content rather than origin; doing otherwise would be the genetic fallacy. Text licensed CC BY 4.0.

Change Log

Version 1.0 → 1.1 (June 2026)

  • Added Section 5.1: Audit of non-natural normative facts (Parfit). Applies the name-the-relata diagnostic directly to irreducibly normative reasons and shows they are the residue, an essence with its relata stripped.
  • Added references r5a (trilemma, TR rev. 5, §6.4) and r5b (Consistency Tax definition, TR rev. 5, T9 and §5.1).
entry.blogger:metaDescription: Every philosophical essence is a relation with its relata stripped: a diagnostic locating ought, number, meaning, and modality inside physics.

entry.title: The Is/Ought Firewall
entry.content:
The Is/Ought Firewall

The consolidated account: the agent-relative ought it protects, what it forbids, and why it is a provisional debt rather than a wall

Position and method note · consolidating Ought Is Local and The Firewall Between Is and Ought Is a Scope Decision

Andraž Đurič

Version 1 · June 2026

What this is. The corpus's consolidated account of the is/ought firewall: what it forbids, what it does not, why it is kept, and why it is provisional rather than permanent. It merges and supersedes two earlier pieces, the clarification Ought Is Local and the method note The Firewall Between Is and Ought Is a Scope Decision; both now point here. It carries more of the underlying defense than either did, and marks what it still defers: the full treatment of persistence as a graded quantity, which belongs to the apex work, and the measurement program for the coupling densities, which is empirical and unfinished. One commitment is foundational, physicalism, that everything is physical or reduces to it; it is named and defended below rather than hidden, and a reader who rejects it will read the firewall differently.

The is/ought firewall in this corpus is routinely misread, including by the AI systems I work with, and the misreading is always the same: that the firewall forbids deriving an ought from an is. It does not. It forbids one specific thing and enforces one specific discipline, and neither is the blanket prohibition people assume. What follows states what does not exist, what is derivable, what the firewall is for, why it is provisional, and what would break the whole account.

The foundation, and what does not exist

One commitment underwrites everything else, and it is not naturalism in the loose sense but physicalism in the strict one: everything that exists is physical, or reduces to the physical. The difference matters. "Natural" leaves room for things that are natural but not physical, such as abstract objects, or the natural-but-non-physical normative facts some moral realists posit, and the corpus allows no such room. Everything, values included, chains down to the physical. That is why the chain in the normative label below ends at thermodynamic constraint, and not at some "natural" fact standing beside it.

This commitment is not a bare posit adopted by choice. It is the most strongly justified position available: the standing conclusion of every successful reduction science has carried out, and the one global hypothesis no counterexample has dislodged. It is defeasible in principle, in that a single thing shown to be real and not physical would bring it down, but the burden of producing one sits with the dissenter, and it has gone unmet for a long time. To reject the commitment is to owe either a reason it is not the best-supported position, or the counterexample itself. Granting it is not a leap; it is following the evidence.

Grant it, and a category of thing disappears. There is no categorical ought: no obligation binding an agent regardless of what that agent is, no "you ought to X" that holds as a free-standing fact about the universe rather than a fact about some particular system. The view from nowhere issues no commands. On this much Hume was right: no categorical ought follows from any descriptive premises, and no quantity of physics will produce one. The corpus grants that inferential point in full. What it refuses is the gloss usually hung on it, that the gap implies a separate, autonomous realm of normative facts standing outside the physical. Physicalism forbids that realm. So the traditional is-ought gap, the one between physical fact and a non-physical ought, is not bridged. It is dissolved: there was never a second realm on the far side to bridge to.

Why an ought is derivable anyway

An ought was never agent-independent to begin with. An ought is always an ought for some agent, and an agent is not outside physics. It is a physical system, coupled to a particular environment, at a particular time. Once you fix the agent and its situation you have fixed a set of is-facts: what this system is, what dissolves it, what sustains it. From those facts, specific oughts follow. Given that a system is the kind of persistence-structure it is, in the conditions it is actually in, some courses run toward dissolution and some away, and that is the ought, stated in full. The ought is not a further fact laid on top of the physics. It is that functional fact, addressed to the agent it concerns.

That last claim is the load-bearing one, and a hostile reader will press on it: "is a persistence-structure" describes, "ought to do what sustains it" prescribes, and you have jumped. The reply has two parts. First, the jump is only a jump if the ought is categorical, and this one is not. It is the consequent of a hypothetical, if the system is to persist, then it ought to do what sustains it, whose antecedent is no chosen goal but a redescription of what a self-maintaining structure is, an is-fact. Hume's law forbids deriving a categorical ought from is; it never forbade the hypothetical kind, which was always derivable. Second, and underneath that, the word "ought" here names the agent-indexed sustaining-relation and adds no further property. "X is what the agent ought to do" is not a claim that some extra quality, oughtness, attaches to X; it says X sustains the agent. That is not a vacuous relabeling. Which actions actually sustain a given agent is a hard empirical question, and the substance the word "ought" once seemed to carry sits there, in the facts, rather than in a property of its own. The objection imagines a second thing, a categorical prescription, that the derivation fails to reach. But that second thing was already denied to exist. There is no failed crossing, because there is no second bank.

This is worth locating precisely, because it is easy to mistake for bedrock. The deflationary reading of "ought" is not itself the foundation. Given physicalism, and once a non-physical normative realm is refused, "ought" can refer to one of two things: the agent-relative sustaining-relation, or nothing at all. The first is deflation; the second is error-theory, the view that ought-talk is systematically empty. The corpus takes the first horn. So two things are committed, physicalism, the foundation, and the choice of deflation over error-theory, and from them the agent-relative ought and the denial of any categorical ought both follow as theorems. Treating the deflationary ought as a foundational truth, something one can only assert, misplaces the foundation one level too high. The justified commitment is physicalism; the ought is derived from it.

The position has a price, and naming it is part of being honest about what is committed. Denying categorical oughts means giving up "wrong, period." There is no act this account can call wrong independent of every agent's persistence conditions; wrongness is always wrongness for an agent, relative to what dissolves it. Someone who holds that certain things are wrong no matter who is asking, as a fact about the universe and not about any agent, is holding exactly the categorical ought that physicalism dissolves, and will not be satisfied by an agent-relative substitute. That dissatisfaction is not a flaw in the argument. It is the cost of the foundation, paid in the open.

What the ought is indexed to

Because the ought is agent-relative, it has content only when its terms are named: which agent, which boundary, which environment, which optimization horizon. Leave any of them unfixed and the ought loses its referent. This matters most for the boundary and the horizon, because persistence, the thing the ought is indexed to, is not a simple on-or-off.

Persistence has a boundary and, above it, a gradient. The boundary is an absorbing barrier, dissolution, the state a system does not return from, and that part is binary: a system is either still itself or it has come apart. Above the boundary lies a gradient of endurance, how far above the barrier a system sits, how much disruption it can absorb before crossing, how long it can expect to last. The boundary is binary; the endurance above it is a matter of degree. An ought indexed to persistence is therefore indexed to a position on that gradient, relative to that barrier, over some horizon. A verdict, in the strong sense the firewall defers, is a claim that a given course raises or lowers expected endurance over the relevant horizon. The full account of persistence as a graded quantity belongs to the apex work; what matters here is that the ought's relata include the barrier it is measured against and the stretch of time over which endurance is reckoned.

The gap that remains is inside physics

The traditional gap is dissolved, but a real gap remains, and it is inside physics. It runs between the agent-blind description of the substrate, gradients and flows that know of no agent, and the agent-relative description, the level at which there is a bounded system, a thing that can persist or fail to. Oughts live at the second level. Reading one off the first, as though the substrate itself prescribed it, is a location error, the same delocalization diagnosed in The Wizard's Error Is Delocalization. The ought is real and it is physical, but it is local: indexed to an agent, a boundary, an environment, a horizon. Lift it out of that index and it does not become purer or more universal, and it does not become false. It becomes contentless, a ghost: a term with the grammar of a claim and no referent, nothing on the far side to be true or false about. The ought was never anywhere but in its index.

The normative, chained. A normative claim in this corpus says what an agent ought to do or value. It is agent-relative and goal-dependent, and the ought is chained to physics through the agent: ought, then the agent's persistence conditions, then the thermodynamic constraint those conditions answer to, never suspended above the physical. The label marks a claim as agent-relative, and in a descriptive document as out of scope. It never licenses reading the ought as a non-natural property floating free of a body. This is the standing of the normative label set in High-Fidelity Maps (§4.4); the present piece is its full statement.

So why keep the firewall

If is yields ought agent-relatively, why keep the firewall at all? Two reasons, and only the first is Hume's.

The first is to hold the index in place: to stop anyone, myself included, from quietly promoting a local ought into a categorical one by forgetting whose ought it was. It is the same name-the-relata discipline the corpus turns on other people's normative claims, turned on its own. An ought asserted with its agent and frame stripped off does not become more general. It becomes a ghost, and the firewall is what flags the ghost before it is taken for a result.

The second reason matters more in practice, and it is not metaphysical at all. It is modeling honesty. The corpus holds, as a bet and not a finished demonstration, that every value worth the name reduces, in content, to persistence. But reduces in principle is not has been reduced. For any specific value, take vitality, the quality of a system that is intensely and coherently alive, the reduction is a model that does not yet exist. It would have to climb every layer from thermodynamics up to the phenomenon, each layer demanding its own empirics, generated and defended and justified. That model is, at present, beyond anything I can build.

Two kinds of model are in play, and they are not at the same maturity. The first-order sciences a verdict would draw on improve in the ordinary way and are not the bottleneck. The apparatus that would integrate them into a persistence verdict, a quantified model of the relevant agent and the couplings inside it, is young. Those couplings, the densities measuring how far one system's states carry predictive information about another's persistence, are at present estimated rather than measured, and the multi-scale models that would output a verdict are work in progress, not finished instruments. So the firewall is not only a budget on length. It marks honest immaturity in the integrating layer, and that is why it is provisional rather than principled.

The firewall keeps two different statements from being confused: that the reduction is guaranteed by the monism, and that it has been carried out. It separates the is-ledger from the ought-ledger, not because they are disconnected, they are not, this is a monism and everything connects, but because claiming the bridge is finished when it is only promised is the overclaim that discredits a framework. The firewall is a debt, not a wall, and at every point where an ought is asserted it records that the descent to the floor remains to be paid in full.

One distinction guards against a tempting shortcut. That values reduce, in content, to persistence is a claim about what values are; it is never a proof that a particular ought holds. The reduction is monist metaphysics; the derivation of a specific ought is agent-relative and instrumental, and runs through the agent's actual conditions. Wheeling the reduction in as a proof of a verdict, as though showing that a value bottoms out in persistence settled what an agent should do, would be a different overclaim, and the firewall blocks it too.

The boundary moves

None of this makes the firewall permanent, or principled in the Humean sense. It marks the current edge of the model actually deployed in a given piece, not a border in reality. As the integrating layer matures and the couplings are measured, the firewall in a given domain can come down, and the verdict becomes derivable from the facts about that agent. Until then, marking the boundary is the honest move. Asserting a verdict across it would not add rigor; it would emit an ought whose relata cannot yet be named to the required precision, which is to say a ghost.

A worked case: The Shape of the Disagreement

The point is sharpest where the integrating layer is least mature. The Shape of the Disagreement is a diagnostic, a piece whose job is to map the structure of a disagreement rather than resolve it. Its firewall separates the empirical crux, what the facts of sex and gender are, from the goal crux, which persistence conditions a categorization scheme should be built to serve. The diagnostic shows that most of the dispute lives at the goal crux, not the fact crux, and stops there.

To go further and derive the categorization a polity ought to adopt, the piece would have to become a different document. It would engage the biology of sex differentiation and the neurology of gender identity at the level those fields demand. It would model the relevant higher-scale agent, the coupled social system whose persistence the policy is indexed to, and put numbers on couplings that are at present estimated, not measured. And it would hold terminology and semantics to the standard any such claim requires, since the conflations the diagnostic identifies are the failure mode a careless derivation would repeat. That is a monograph doing several jobs at once. The diagnostic does one, and marks where it ends.

Two clarifications

The floor is thermodynamics, not because nothing lies beneath it, but because thermodynamics is the lowest level from which we can actually model upward into complexity. Whatever sits below, quantum or otherwise, we cannot yet build the ladder from there; we build it from here. Thermodynamics is the functional floor, not the metaphysical one.

And two claims often treated as rivals are not rivals. That all values reduce to persistence, and that persistence is the precondition for valuing anything at all, do not compete: the first entails the second, so granting the precondition never costs the reduction, and reading them as a forced choice is a mistake. Whether the reduction actually goes through for any given value is the separate, mostly unpaid question above. The compatibility is secure; the reduction is the bet. There is one floor, and the two theses meet at it.

What would break this

Several claims here are open to refutation, and naming what would refute them is part of holding them honestly.

The structural claim, that there is no categorical ought and every ought is agent-relative, would be broken by a single counterexample: an obligation that binds independent of any agent's constitution, derivable from descriptive facts alone, with no agent in its index. No such ought has been produced, and the deflationary account predicts none can be; but the prediction is refutable, and that is what keeps it a claim rather than a posture.

The reduction bet, that every value reduces in content to persistence, would be broken by a value that, once fully modeled, demonstrably does not, one whose content bottoms out in something orthogonal to persistence rather than in persistence itself. The dissolution floor, where values that destroy their holder are ruled out, is the trivial end of the reduction and is already secure; the bet is that the pattern continues up. A modeled value that reduced to a thermodynamic quantity other than persistence, or to nothing physical at all, would break it.

Beneath both sits the foundation's own break-condition: any real thing shown to be non-physical brings down physicalism, and with it everything built on physicalism here. That is the deepest refutation available, and the one the whole record of reduction has so far kept unmet.

Standing of this document. This is a position and method note, not a result, and its parts do not have the same status; the firewall exists partly to keep that visible. Physicalism is the foundation, the most strongly justified position available and defeasible only by a non-physical counterexample, not a free choice. The denial of categorical oughts and the agent-relative, deflationary ought are theorems from it, together with the choice of deflation over error-theory. The graded structure of persistence is a characterization, sharpened here and fully treated elsewhere. That every value reduces in content to persistence is a live bet, far more speculative than the foundation and mostly uncomputed, with the failure point named above. That the integrating layer will mature enough for the firewall to retract in a given domain is a second live bet, empirical and unfinished. Corrections and counterexamples are welcome and change the note.

A note on the word "settled," because it does two jobs that must not be run together. When the structural claim is called settled, that marks it as held fixed while one works inside it, not as closed to revision. It is the best-supported standing position, revisable in principle by a counterexample, but not relitigated mid-argument and not what the firewall is waiting on. What the firewall is waiting on is the integrating model and the measured couplings, and that is open in the ordinary, empirical way.

References

  1. Hume, D. (1739–1740). A Treatise of Human Nature, Book III, Part I, Section I. The is-to-ought passage: the source of the inferential point the corpus grants, and the target of the autonomous-realm gloss it refuses. Standard
  2. Nagel, T. (1986). The View from Nowhere. Oxford University Press. Source of the phrase used here for the agent-independent standpoint that issues no oughts. Standard

Author: Andraž Đurič, independent researcher, Slovenia. This piece consolidates and supersedes Ought Is Local and The Firewall Between Is and Ought Is a Scope Decision. Written in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic), following an earlier exchange with another language model. Contributions are judged on content rather than origin; doing otherwise would be the genetic fallacy. Text licensed CC BY 4.0.

entry.title: The Exclusivity Error
entry.content:
The Exclusivity Error

Understanding the bricks makes the castle more real, not less

Essay · levels, reduction, and the demand that a high-level term name its referent

Andraž Đurič

Version 1 · June 2026

There is a recurring move in how people argue, and it is an error: treating an explanation at one level as if it cancelled the thing at every other. Love is "just" neurochemistry. A symphony is "just" pressure waves. Justice is "just" group dynamics. Call it the exclusivity error: the belief that to explain a thing at one level is to explain it away at all the others.

The castle

Take a Lego castle. Every brick is acrylonitrile butadiene styrene, a polymer whose behavior is fixed by the covalent bonds between its atoms. The chemistry is exactly true. The castle still stands. Knowing the substrate did not flatten the structure into a formula; it added a floor to what you can see — the architecture on one level, the polymer on the level below, the first held up by the second. You have not lost the castle. You can now see one more floor of it.

The stack is real

Reality is layered this way the whole way up: physics, chemistry, biology, psychology, the social, the normative. Each level has its own regularities and its own vocabulary, and the higher ones are not abolished by the lower ones that realize them. This is not a new thought. It is ordinary non-reductive physicalism: that more is different (Anderson), that the special sciences are not biding time until they dissolve into physics (Fodor), that a higher-level pattern is real exactly when tracking it earns its keep (Dennett). The error is not studying one level. The error is the extra step of insisting that yours is the only one that is real.

Specialization is forced. No mind holds every level at full resolution at once, so each of us zooms in somewhere. But zooming in is not the error. The error is the further claim that the floors you zoomed away from were never really there.

Where Name the Relata gets misread

This is where my own diagnostic, Name the Relata, gets read backwards. It is not eliminativism, not a demand to abandon the upper floors and speak only about persistence dynamics in the basement. But it is not the soft, ecumenical view either, the one where every floor is fine and we are all simply to be courteous to each other across them. It makes a specific and asymmetric demand: a level-term — "ought," "justice," "authority" — carries a debt. It has to be redeemable against some real relatum: a real agent, a real system, the thing the term is about. The relatum need not live in the basement. It can sit on any floor. What it cannot do is fail to exist. A term that cannot name what it is relative to is not a high-level truth; it is furniture arranged in a room with no building under it. Name the Relata is the formal statement of that demand; this essay is the plain one.

Two commitments, and they pull in opposite directions on purpose. Explaining a level does not abolish it: do not collapse justice into chemistry. Invoking a level-term commits you to a referent: do not invoke justice with nothing it is the justice of. The first protects the upper floors from reduction. The second makes them pay rent.

The work is at the interface

The real work is at the interfaces, in the translation between one level's vocabulary and another's, which is where the difficulty actually lives and where neither the reductionist nor the holist is at ease. Understanding what the bricks are made of does not diminish the castle. It tells you what is holding it up.

References

  1. Anderson, P. W. (1972). More Is Different. Science 177(4047), 393–396. The levels point: higher-level organization is not abolished by, nor a mere restatement of, the laws below it. Verified · June 2026
  2. Fodor, J. A. (1974). Special Sciences (or: The Disunity of Science as a Working Hypothesis). Synthese 28(2), 97–115. The autonomy of the special sciences: their laws are not biding time until a reduction to physics. Verified · June 2026
  3. Dennett, D. C. (1991). Real Patterns. The Journal of Philosophy 88(1), 27–51. A higher-level pattern counts as real when registering it compresses description; the criterion behind "earns its keep." Verified · June 2026
  4. Name the Relata (June 2026). The formal statement of the asymmetric anchoring demand this essay puts plainly; internal, existing on this blog. Internal

Author: Andraž Đurič, Slovenia. The levels picture is ordinary non-reductive physicalism, used illustratively rather than claimed as new; the asymmetric anchoring demand is the corpus's, stated here in plain register. Written in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic); contributions are judged on content, not origin. Text licensed CC BY 4.0.
